newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha shrugs off firmer crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha shrugs off firmer crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were little changed on Friday, shrugging off overnight crude gains, as bearish sentiment overhung the market amid ample prompt supplies, traders said.
Second-half June open-spec naphtha was bid at $208.50 to $209.00 per tonne while offers were assessed $1.00 higher.
First-half June contract was sold to a European trader at $207.50 in late Thursday dealing.
Near-term spreads remained in contango, with first-half June contract quoted about $1.00 lower than the second-half of the month.
Inter-delivery spreads were assessed in backwardation from first-half July onwards, with first-half July/first-half August indicated at plus $1.50 to $2.00.
Naphtha spreads for near-term trading periods are expected to remain in contango until the supply and demand balance in Asia tightens, traders said.

They estimated that more than 300,000 tonnes of physical cargoes remained available for second-half May and early June delivery in the region, while Japanese end-users' demand for second-half May has mostly been covered.
